title: Exogenous creatine supplementation promotes tumor metastasis via megakaryocyte creatine kinase B-STAT5B signaling
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-74639-z

How diet regulates cancer progression and therapeutic response is not completely understood. Here, the authors show that creatine supplementation promotes tumor metastasis by inducing hyperactive platelets in cancer models.

title: Direct coupling of nod factor signaling to vesicular trafficking initiates legume nodulation
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75535-2

Soybean plants initiate symbiosis with nitrogen-fixing bacteria by remodeling cell membranes. This study shows that bacterial signals activate a receptor that switches on a membrane fusion protein, enabling infection thread and nodule formation.

title: Profiling the gut resistome to unlock antimicrobial resistance biology and inform clinical risk
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 15 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75659-5

The gut microbiome contains a vast reservoir of antimicrobial resistance genes. In this Review, the authors discuss how gut resistome profiling is advancing understanding of resistance biology while creating new opportunities for surveillance, clinical risk prediction and antimicrobial stewardship.

title: Self-heating-induced blocking in nanopores enables neuromorphic ionic computing
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75570-z

The prospects of fluidic memristors in neuromorphic computing fuel demand for new memristive devices. Here, Fan et al. show a self-heating-induced blocking memristor achieving multiple neuromorphic functions.

title: Potential-mediated enol-keto equilibrium in phenol electro-hydrogenation on platinum
abstract:
Nature Communications, Published online: 14 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75401-1

Electrocatalytic hydrogenation of phenol provides valuable chemicals, but the origin of selective cyclohexanone formation remains elusive. Here, the author report that cathodic polarization drives enol–keto tautomerization, trapping cyclohexanone in a floating state for selective accumulation.
